newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber steady, no default impact so far.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber steady, no default impact so far.

text.p: Thai rubber was steady to higher as the rallies in the Tokyo market overshadowed the impact of a Thai government default on a 23,100-tonne purchase, dealers said on Friday.
But the overall market remained thin this week with China and Japan featuring as key buyers.
"The Chinese bought around 20,000 tonnes so far this month. Not too bad," said a Bangkok-based dealer.
Other traders said the baht volatility also dampened business. The Thai baht plunged to a record-low of 32.70 baht per dollar on Thursday.
"Players don't know what the valuation of the baht should be since it's very volatile, so they became very cautious," said another traders.
"The prices were up mostly because of higher Tokyo prices following the expiry of spot July," he said.
Traders said the currency volatility and the government defaults were likely to weigh on the market until next week.
The government decided on Thursday not to accept the delivery of the rubber which it purchased from local exporters to cut losses as rubber prices continued their downtrend.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for September delivery was offered at 95.00 US cents a kg free on board Bangkok and December at 99.00 cents on the same basis.
